LIVE PROOF for the C13 timing-relief loop (orch #651 arms relief, #655 structural cut/merge/reallocate). The relief loop shortens an OVER-BUDGET timeline; until now its only live trace was a `timeline_manifest=` STRING inside reconcile_timeline.notes[], which scripts/e2e_validate.py cannot parse — so the loop was provable only by the deterministic unit test tests/services/stages/demo_video/test_reconcile_timeline_structural.py, never by the e2e harness. This scenario asserts on the NEW typed `timeline_manifest` field (added to DemoVideoGenOutput) so a live run proves loop_iterations>=1 AND converged.

OVER-BUDGET / ELASTIC DESIGN (why it converges): authored mode (brief.lines) gives EXACT control over the spine. The three lines are PURE VOICEOVER beats — no `clip`, no `claim_status`, no `locked`/`time_lock` — so every beat is UNPROTECTED and fully ELASTIC (elasticity 1.0). A VO beat's demand floor is words/wpm_max*60 = words/170*60. With word counts 40/30/25 the AUTHORED floors are 14.12s + 10.59s + 8.82s = 33.53s.

DOCTOR-DECOUPLED TARGETS (2026-09-02 — read this before touching either number). The authored counts are NOT what reconcile_timeline sees: `script_doctor` runs FIRST and REWRITES these lines, and it is steered by the DELIVERABLE's `target_duration_seconds`, so its OUTPUT length is a function of THAT knob, not of how many words were authored. MEASURED across all four live runs of this scenario (2026-08-27 / 08-28 / 08-31 / 09-02), 95 authored words came back as 61 / 68 / 61 / 56 doctored words -> floors of 21.53s / 24.00s / 21.53s / 19.76s. Against the ORIGINAL `target_seconds: 20` that is a COIN FLIP: three runs stayed infeasible and the gate passed, and the fourth (matrix run 33590213252, orchestrator run 01a06087-f83b-7153-908c-acce5a5cd25a) trimmed to 19.76s <= 20s -> the timeline was FEASIBLE, `infeasible_beats()` was empty, relief CORRECTLY never armed, `timeline_manifest` was null, and a perfectly healthy product RED-ed the matrix on LLM trim variance alone. Two obvious repairs are both WRONG: authoring EVEN LONGER lines does nothing (the doctor rewrites to its own target regardless of input length — 95 words in, 56-68 words out either way), and LOWERING the deliverable's `target_duration_seconds` makes it STRICTLY WORSE (that is the very knob the doctor chases). THE FIX IS TO DECOUPLE THE TWO TARGETS, which the code already permits: `script_doctor._resolve_target` reads ONLY the deliverable `target_duration_seconds` (shared/script_doctor.py), while reconcile_timeline's target ladder PREFERS `direction.timing.target_seconds` and only falls back to the deliverable (reconcile_timeline.py `_resolve_timing_config`). So the deliverable STAYS at 20s — the doctor keeps aiming at a ~20s script — and the RELIEF target drops to 8s. Margin: the doctor's own aim point is 20 * 150/170 = 17.65s of floor (its rubric budgets words at _WPM=150, reconcile floors them at wpm_max=170), i.e. 2.2x above the 8s relief target, and the DEEPEST trim ever measured (56 words = 19.76s) is 2.47x above it. To make this premise false the doctor would have to emit <= 22 words TOTAL across three lines (~7 words each) — below every per-line count ever observed (minimum 16) and below its own rubric's length floors. RE-MEASURE these numbers if script_doctor's rubric, target resolution, or model changes; the static guard that pins the margin is tests/test_e2e_scenario_contracts.py::test_a_relief_premise_survives_the_script_doctor.

So Sum(min) is comfortably > 8s -> infeasible_beats() is non-empty -> the opt-in relief loop ARMS (relief.mode=auto). The timing-director can honestly SHORTEN or CUT/MERGE these unprotected elastic beats. Because EVERY beat is unprotected the protected floor is 0s <= 8s, so `_classify_convergence` can never return `cant_converge` here and no structural-relief CHILD RUN is ever spawned by this scenario; cutting down to the shortest surviving beat leaves ~5.6s <= 8s, so a re-solved timeline can still be FEASIBLE and the solver water-fills the freed seconds into the survivors. relief.score_threshold is set to 3.0 (not the 4.0 default): the moment the timeline is feasible the pacing-critic scores it in the 3.0-5.0 band, so best_score>=3.0 -> LoopResult.converged=True regardless of the rhythm read. A pure footage-pinned spine provably CANNOT converge (footage cut/merge is protected/rejected), which is exactly why these beats carry NO clip.

ASSERTIONS (deliberately ROBUST, not LLM-flaky): `numeric_gte timeline_manifest.run.loop_iterations >= 1` proves the relief loop ARMED and ran (loop-engine `passes` is >=1 whenever the loop runs; pass 1 = initial draft). `in timeline_manifest.run.convergence_outcome ["converged", "progress"]` (STRENGTHENED from `nonempty` 2026-09-13 — see the RESIDUAL HOLE CLOSED note in `_checks_doc`) proves #671's honest classifier POPULATED the typed manifest live WITH A SUCCESS OUTCOME, where `nonempty` accepted the crash literal `relief_failed` — timeline_manifest is `| None` and set only on a relief run, so a non-empty convergence_outcome establishes that the relief+classification path (orch #670/#671) executed end-to-end on the live cluster. Together they are the live proof that the machinery is wired and functioning. NOTE the earlier `converged >= 1` check was DROPPED on purpose: these three beats are unprotected/elastic (trim-eligible, no clip/claim/lock), so the structural prepass returns them unchanged and feasibility rests on the IN-PLACE trim loop shrinking the DOCTORED spine (56-68 words measured) to <=22 words in <=2 passes — an outcome of the live timing-director LLM's trim quality (a #651/#655-era property), NOT of #670/#671. Asserting converged=true live would red a working feature whenever the small director under-trims; the AUTHORITATIVE convergence proof is therefore the deterministic unit test tests/services/stages/demo_video/test_reconcile_timeline_structural.py (stubbed director), which this live gate supplements, not replaces.

LIVE PREREQUISITE (how record reaches reconcile_timeline): reconcile_timeline runs AFTER demo_video_record. This is a PURE-VO authored spine (brief.lines only, no `clip`), so demo_video_gen emits bdd_job_id="" and no package_url — i.e. there is NO footage SOURCE. As of the 2026-07-24 record-degrade hardening, demo_video_record DEGRADES on a footage-acquisition failure (no package_url and no bdd_job_id → nothing to record; likewise a terminal frontend_test_runner job failure) instead of hard-raising: it returns empty clips + a footage-gap note, `runs/_shared.py` translates the note into a `degraded` run, and the beats stay fully elastic (nothing pins them). So the run reaches reconcile_timeline and the relief loop arms + converges on the cuttable VO beats. `target_url` is required by record's input contract but is INERT on the no-source path (FTR is never called). Because these beats have no footage, downstream compile has no video for them; this scenario is DISPATCH/NIGHTLY-only (never gates promote) and its authoritative purpose is the reconcile_timeline manifest assertion. After any change to this spec DISPATCH the workflow and read the reconcile_timeline stage output before calling it green (see w2v_orchestrator/CLAUDE.md validation-strategy note).

_targets_deliberately_decoupled: DELIBERATE, 2026-09-02. `direction.timing.target_seconds` (8) and the deliverable's `target_duration_seconds` (20) are NOT the same knob and must NOT be made to agree here. reconcile_timeline budgets against the 8, and `script_doctor` steers its rewrite against the 20 — so holding the deliverable HIGH is what stops the doctor trimming this spine feasible and disarming the relief loop this scenario exists to prove. See the DOCTOR-DECOUPLED TARGETS paragraph in `_doc` for the four measured runs and the 2.2x margin. Making these two numbers equal (as they were until 2026-09-02) reinstates the coin-flip red.
_checks_doc:
STRENGTHENED 2026-09-05, but deliberately NOT by pinning convergence_outcome — read this before 'finishing the job' by copying the twin.

WHAT WAS ADDED. (a) `status: "completed"` — the spec omitted the stage status entirely, so reconcile_timeline could have been any status at all and the checks were still evaluated against whatever output it left. (b) `equals timeline_manifest.run.protected_beat_count == 0` (TimelineManifestRun.protected_beat_count, shared/time_budget.py:670, populated at reconcile_timeline.py:2075 from `sum(1 for line in lines if _is_protected(line, final_footage_ids))`). That is 0 BY CONSTRUCTION here: the three authored beats carry no `clip`, no `claim_status` and no `locked`/`time_lock`, which is the premise the whole `_doc` above rests on. Pinning it turns a silent premise-invalidation into a NAMED failure — exactly the defect class that reddened this scenario on 2026-09-02 and its twin on the same matrix — and it also makes `cant_converge` unreachable-and-asserted, since _classify_convergence can only return cant_converge when the PROTECTED floor exceeds the target and a zero protected floor never does.

WHY convergence_outcome IS NOT PINNED TO A LITERAL. The twin demo_video_footage_relief can assert `equals "cant_converge"` because footage-pinned beats make that outcome deterministic. Here it is NOT: the `_doc` above documents four measured live runs in which the honest outcome swings between `converged` and `progress` purely on how hard the timing-director LLM trims the doctored spine, and it records that the earlier `converged >= 1` check was dropped for precisely that reason. `equals` is the only literal check the engine has (e2e_validate.py::_eval_check supports equals / numeric_gte / distinct_count_gte / nonempty — there is no set-membership or negation form), so pinning either literal would red a healthy run about half the time. Left as `nonempty`.

RESIDUAL HOLE CLOSED 2026-09-13. It used to read: `nonempty` still accepts `"relief_failed"` — the outcome emitted when the relief loop RAISED (shared/time_budget.py:639-644) — so a CRASHED relief loop that still emits a manifest read GREEN on the one check this scenario exists to make. That is exactly the vacuous shape this corpus keeps producing: an assertion that the pipeline said SOMETHING, not that it said something good. The doc above correctly recorded why `equals` could not close it (the honest outcome swings `converged` <-> `progress` across four measured live runs, so pinning either literal reds a healthy run about half the time) and then concluded the engine offered nothing better. It now does: `in` (scripts/e2e_validate.py::_eval_in) takes an ALLOW-LIST of SUCCESS values, so the check is `in ["converged", "progress"]` — both honest outcomes pass, `relief_failed` fails, and so does every future failure literal nobody has seen yet, because the list is an allow-list rather than a deny-list. The rejected `pacing_score >= 0` workaround is moot and stays rejected.
